newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper called to open steady-to-firm.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper called to open steady-to-firm.

text.p: COMEX copper futures were seen opening steady to firm Wednesday, in line with LME copper, as the market recovered from Tuesday's slippage.
COMEX July copper was seen opening unchanged to up 0.20 cent a pound from Tuesday close at 121.20 cents, after trading in a 120.35-121.45 cent range in overnight ACCESS trade.
Support is seen around 120 cents still, with resistance around the contract high seen last week at 122.90 cents.

LME warehouse copper stocks rose 300 tonnes to 122,525 tonnes in Wednesday's data, following a steady decline in recent week, while COMEX copper stocks were up 251 short tons at 48,961 short tons Tuesday.
LME copper stocks have fallen steadily from 145,750 tonnes at the start of May and from around 200,000 tonnes at the start of the year, reflecting a tightening supply situation, analysts said.
In other news, unions representing striking workers at Inco Limited's Sudbury operations in Canada, wanted to restart talks with the company as the walk-out entered its third week.
Inco, the world's biggest nickel producer, also produces copper which is sold in northeastern U.S.
